pages.lesson:
LESSON: HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.3: Handwriting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Handwriting. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you take care of classroom items?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary on colours for language acquisition
2. write simple sentences using descriptive words in neat and legible handwriting
3. appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HANDWRITING
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Handwriting helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: HANDWRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary on colours for language acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary on colours for language acquisition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary on colours for language acquisition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary on colours for language acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write simple sentences using descriptive words in neat and legible handwriting

What this means
In this part you learn to write simple sentences using descriptive words in neat and legible handwriting. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write simple sentences using descriptive words in neat and legible handwriting.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Handwriting to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write simple sentences using descriptive words in neat and legible handwriting. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Handwriting is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Handwriting”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary on colours for language acquisition)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Handwriting to a partner. (skill: write simple sentences using descriptive words in neat and legible handwriting)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Handwriting to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary on colours for language acquisition.
3. Practise this skill: write simple sentences using descriptive words in neat and legible handwriting.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the skill of writing for effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Handwriting from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Handwriting: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Handwriting?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you take care of classroom items?
2. Why is neat handwriting preferred in writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Handwriting means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary on colours for language acquisition.
5. Be able to: write simple sentences using descriptive words in neat and legible handwriting.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
